blocks.content: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280, whereas the Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body established by executive resolution.

rows: Created by Executive Cabinet Resolution in 1950
Formulation of Five-Year Plans & resource allocation

items: Article 280 governs the Finance Commission; remember that its recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding.
The Planning Commission had no constitutional provision and was created by a cabinet resolution, unlike the statutory or constitutional status of other bodies.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on January 1, 2015, shifting focus from top-down planning to cooperative federalism.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body defined under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, constituted by the President every five years.
The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, extra-constitutional body established via an executive resolution in March 1950.
The Finance Commission mainly deals with tax revenue distribution between the Union and States, and determining grants-in-aid.
The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating India's Five-Year Plans and making plan resource allocations to states.
On 1st January 2015, the Planning Commission was officially replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).
